newsitem.title: USA: Republicans to invite Clinton to meet lawmakers.
newsitem.headline: Republicans to invite Clinton to meet lawmakers.

text.p: Senate Majority leader Trent Lott said on Sunday that Republican lawmakers planned to invite President Clinton to Capitol Hill for a bipartisan meeting to discuss the budget, education, crime and other key issues.

"Let's begin to talk seriously about areas where we do have some degree of agreement," the Mississippi Republican told ABC television's "This Week" news program. "Let's start working on that. We know where we disagree," he added.
It was not completely clear from Lott's comments whether the Republicans would propose that the meeting be held this Wednesday or the following one.
Clinton is scheduled to go to Augusta, Georgia, this Wednesday to press his plans for improving education.
Lott said the meeting would not be designed just to discuss the budget.
"This is not just a budget talk," he said.

"This is sort of sit down and say, 'Mr. President, it's time that we stopped the little pigeon steps around here and let's begin to see what we can really do to move things forward for the American people.'"
